subject: Adding a legend to the graph with ggplot2

messages.author: d94528fc2510e36a
messages.subject: Adding a legend to the graph with ggplot2
parts:
Hi, 

   In the ggplot2 manual, it seems to say that legend emerges automatically (I might be wrong; please correct me). However, I could not see the legend in my graph. Could someone add a few lines in my graph so that I might see the legend on the top of the graph? 

   Thanks, 

Miao 


rm(list=ls())
library(ggplot2)

x1<-1:4
y1<-6:9
x2<-1:3
y2<-5:7
dft01<-data.frame(x1,y1)
dft02<-data.frame(x2,y2)
p1<-ggplot(dft01, aes(x=x1, y=y1))+
  geom_point(shape = 19, color="blue") +
  geom_point(shape=3,aes(x=x2, y=y2),data=dft02, color="red")+
  theme_bw()
p2<-p1+theme(legend.position="top")
p2

  you have to restructe your data.

rm(list=ls())
library(ggplot2)

x1<-1:4
y1<-6:9
x2<-1:3
y2<-5:7

dft01<-data.frame(x=x1,y=y1,df=factor("df1",levels=c("df1","df2")))
dft02<-data.frame(x=x2,y=y2,df=factor("df2",levels=c("df1","df2")))
dft <- rbind(dft01,dft02)
qplot(x,y,shape=df,color=df,data=dft)+ theme(legend.position="top")

Robert

messages.author: 5ec5102a43e29af7
messages.subject: Re: Adding a legend to the graph with ggplot2
parts:
Hi Miao,


you need to 'map' some variable of your dataset to an aesthetic
component of ggplot, then the legend emerges automatically.

e.g.

dft01 <- data.frame(x=x1,y=y1,c='one')
dft02 <- data.frame(x=x2,y=y2,c='two')
dat <- rbind(dft01,dft02)

p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x=x,y=y, colour=c)) + geom_point()
print(p)

Default colors can then be changed by

p + scale_colour_manual('Legend:', values = c('one'='red','two'='blue'))

Other aesthetics like shape, size, ... can be changed accordingly.

cheers,
stefan

parts:
Hi, 

   Thanks very much for your reply. Now I want to change both shapes and colors and let the legend emerge. I modify the codes as below. The plot is ok, but two sets of legends emerge. One is with default colors and specified shapes, while the other is with default shapes and specified colors. Could someone fix it so that the legend emerges correctly? Thanks,

Miao 



rm(list=ls())
library(ggplot2)

x1<-1:4
y1<-6:9
x2<-1:3
y2<-5:7

dft01 <- data.frame(x=x1,y=y1,c='one')
dft02 <- data.frame(x=x2,y=y2,c='two')


dat <- rbind(dft01,dft02)

#p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x=x,y=y, colour=c)) + geom_point()
p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x=x,y=y, colour=c, shape=c)) + geom_point()
print(p)

#Default colors can then be changed by

p + 
  scale_colour_manual('Legend:', values = c('one'='red','two'='blue'))+
  scale_shape_manual(values=c('one'=19,'two'=3))
